claims.text: Optimized PBF-LB processing will produce a highly compositionally homogeneous W20Mo20Ta20Nb20V20 refractory HEA.
Optimized PBF-LB processing will produce a single-phase BCC microstructure.
Optimized PBF-LB processing will minimize porosity and other process-induced defects.
Optimized PBF-LB processing will reduce residual stresses.
The optimized material will have greater ductility under dynamic impact loading than conventionally or non-optimally processed material.
The optimized material will deform more uniformly under dynamic impact loading than the baseline material.
The optimized material will retain its high compressive strength.
The optimized material will retain rapid impact-induced energy-release capability.
Conventionally manufactured refractory HEAs often have heterogeneous microstructures.
Conventionally manufactured refractory HEAs often contain significant porosity.
Conventionally manufactured refractory HEAs often contain significant residual stresses.
Conventionally manufactured refractory HEAs often contain compositional inhomogeneities.

W20Mo20Ta20Nb20V20 can be fabricated by PBF-LB through in-situ alloy formation with complete powder fusion and without a significant number of undissolved particles when favorable parameters are selected.
Optimization of laser power, scan speed, and hatch spacing can ensure a relative density above 99.5%.
The high cooling rates of PBF-LB can mitigate elemental segregation during solidification.
Adjusting PBF-LB process parameters and scan strategies permits precise control of energy input and thereby management of cooling conditions.
Suppressing defects and compositional inhomogeneity reduces localized stress concentrations.
The optimized homogeneous and low-defect microstructure promotes uniform dislocation mobility.
More uniform dislocation mobility enhances ductility and uniform deformation while preserving high strength.
A dynamic strain rate of approximately 3000 s^-1 suitably simulates impact conditions for this alloy.
